answer: One identity claims one mesa ledge, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a key-bound raven nest record with nest material and ledge tag. An auditor checks the ledge at nadir, the nightly low hour, and recomputes the record against the mesa nest table; an empty ledge, reused tag, or material mismatch burns the bond. The first filing is 34 credits, the kth 34+6(k-1), so the 1000th is 6028; 1000 fakes pay 3,031,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-nest ring fails: one tag cannot cover two ledges at nadir. An honest identity pays 34 once and recovers its bond after a clean check.
